# Other Node.js Core Modules

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Smaller or lower-priority Node built-in modules, grouped here rather than given a full page each. Split out to its own page (rather than [PROCESS-CLI.md](PROCESS-CLI.md)) once it's substantial enough to need one.

**Coverage**: 16/17 (~94%) · **Strict Coverage**: 1/17 (~6%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Module | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `querystring` | ✅ | • Repeated keys collapse to the last value instead of an array — `.parse('a=1&a=3')` yields `{a:'3'}`, not Node's `{a:['1','3']}` | • Surface: `.parse`, `.stringify`<br>• A `Map<string,string>` in, out — the same shape `req.query`/`URLSearchParams` already use<br>• `.parse` doesn't strip a leading `?` (matching real Node; distinct from `new URLSearchParams(str)`, which does) |
| `assert` | ✅ | • `equal`/`strictEqual` and `deepEqual`/`deepStrictEqual` (and their `not*` counterparts) are aliases of each other — this compiler's `==` has no implicit coercion to distinguish them<br>• `deepStrictEqual`: Map/Set/class instances, nullable-scalar members, and TypedArrays are a clean compile error (V1)<br>• `.match`/`.doesNotMatch`'s regexp argument must be statically a RegExp ([ADR-00428](../adr/ADR-00428.md))<br>• `.throws` only checks that *something* was thrown, not the thrown value's type/message<br>• No `assert.rejects`/`doesNotReject` (needs await-a-rejection machinery) and no `AssertionError` class ([ADR-00499](../adr/ADR-00499.md)) | • Surface: `.ok`, bare `assert(cond, msg?)`, `.equal`/`.strictEqual`, `.notEqual`/`.notStrictEqual`, `.deepEqual`/`.deepStrictEqual` (+`not*`), `.fail`, `.throws`, `.doesNotThrow`, `.ifError`, `.match`/`.doesNotMatch`<br>• `deepStrictEqual` covers scalars, strings, arrays, and objects (recursively, incl. nested) |
| `test` / `node:test` | ✅ | • **Run-at-registration**: top-level code after a `test()` runs after it here, before it in Node. See [TDD-00140](../tdd/TDD-00140.md), [ADR-00419](../adr/ADR-00419.md)<br>• `beforeEach`/`afterEach` are single slots (last wins) and also fire for subtests<br>• No `mock.*`, `t.plan`, `run()`, concurrency, or snapshots<br>• `mustCall` rejects rest-parameter callbacks (a rest tail is not a fixed ABI slot list) ([ADR-00496](../adr/ADR-00496.md))<br>• `mustNotCall()` returns a `() => void`; using it where a non-zero-arity callback is expected is a type mismatch<br>• `mustSucceed` is count-only (the "err is falsy" check is deferred); `expectWarning` runs the thunk but doesn't capture warnings | • Surface: the **runner**: `test`/`it`, `describe`/`suite`, TestContext `t.test`/`t.after`/`t.skip`/`t.todo`/`t.diagnostic`, hooks `before`/`after`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach` — plus the native helpers `mustCall`/`mustCallAtLeast`/`mustNotCall`/`skip`/`expectsError` + env probes<br>• `mustCall` wraps every fixed callback signature — arrays, nullable scalars, any arity ([ADR-00496](../adr/ADR-00496.md))<br>• `import { mustCall } from 'test'` — a first-class builtin (not Node's internal `../common`). `mustCall(fn, n=1)` — plus Node's function-less `mustCall()`/`mustCall(n)` forms, which count a synthesized noop ([ADR-00423](../adr/ADR-00423.md)) — wraps `fn` so its invocation count is verified at process exit (via the existing exit sink); an unmet/exceeded count prints a diagnostic and exits non-zero, giving examples/tests real async assertions instead of `console.log`. See [TDD-00122](../tdd/TDD-00122.md)/[ADR-00370](../adr/ADR-00370.md)<br>• Distinct from `console.assert` (see [CONSOLE.md](CONSOLE.md)) — throws a catchable `AssertionError` (kind-tagged as a base `Error`, since this compiler's fixed error-kind enum has no dedicated slot) instead of logging and continuing |
| `util` | ✅ | • No `.promisify` — the callback builtins (`zlib.gzip`, `child_process.exec`) are name-dispatched calls, not first-class function values to wrap; importing `promisify` fails cleanly ([ADR-00325](../adr/ADR-00325.md))<br>• `.format` requires a string-**literal** format (compile-time walk); a runtime format string is a compile error<br>• `.inspect`'s options object is accepted but ignored (no `depth`/`colors`) | • Surface: `.inspect`, `.format`<br>• `.inspect` reuses the same value formatter as `console.log` (strings single-quoted, `ClassName { … }`, arrays, `10n`)<br>• `.format`: `%s`/`%d`/`%i`/`%f`/`%j`/`%o`/`%O`/`%%`, excess args appended space-separated, unrecognized specifiers left literal — matching Node |
| `net` | ✅ | • `net.connect` uses a **blocking** `connect()` — a slow/unreachable host blocks the event loop until the OS connect timeout ([ADR-00328](../adr/ADR-00328.md))<br>• A connect failure **throws** a catchable `Error` rather than emitting an async `'error'` event<br>• Server binds IPv4 `0.0.0.0` only — no `host`/`path`/options object on `listen`<br>• IPv4-native bind: an accepted socket reports `127.0.0.1` where Node's dual-stack default reports `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, and the server reports `IPv4`/`0.0.0.0` not `IPv6`/`::`<br>• IPC `{ path }` Unix-domain socket: Linux path-layout unverified (Mac-verified only) ([ADR-00588](../adr/ADR-00588.md))<br>• No `'error'`/`'close'`/`'connect'` events on server or socket yet<br>• `setEncoding`/`ref`/`unref`/`pause`/`resume`/`setTimeout` are accepted but no-ops<br>• No back-pressure: `.write` never returns `false` and there's no `'drain'` event<br>• Listeners must be arrow/function-expression literals<br>• `net.Server`/`net.Socket` are not exposed as constructible classes<br>• Socket `'close'` fires with no `hadError` argument, and `'error'` listeners stay a rejection — the runtime's failure paths throw instead of emitting ([ADR-00501](../adr/ADR-00501.md)) | • Surface: TCP server: `net.createServer`, `server.listen`/`address()`/`on('connection'\|'listening')`/`close`; TCP client: `net.connect`/`createConnection` (positional or `{ port, host }`); connection socket `.on('data'\|'end'\|'close'\|'connect'/'ready')`/`.write`/`.end`/`.address()`/`.destroy()`/`.setNoDelay()`/`.setKeepAlive()`; `net.isIP`/`isIPv4`/`isIPv6`<br>• Accept loop and per-connection read pipes fold into the same `select()` event loop as `child_process` ([ADR-00324](../adr/ADR-00324.md)); a client socket reuses the same machinery once connected. A plausible base for a future `WebSocket` (see [NETWORKING.md](NETWORKING.md))<br>• `address()` reads the real bound address+port via `getsockname`+`inet_ntop`, making the `listen(0)` ephemeral-port idiom (`listen(0, () => net.connect(server.address().port, …))`) usable; `net.isIP` parses via `inet_pton` (0/4/6) ([ADR-00397](../adr/ADR-00397.md)/[ADR-00399](../adr/ADR-00399.md))<br>• `'data'` delivers a Buffer; `.write`/`.end` take a string/Buffer/ArrayBuffer/DataView<br>• `.address()` reports the real bound `{ family: "IPv4", address, port }` via `getsockname` — `0.0.0.0` for a server, the real local IP for a connected socket<br>• `net.connect` accepts every positional arity (`(port)`, `(port, cb)`, `(port, host[, cb])`) and `{ port, host }` (host defaults to `localhost`); `on('listening')` fires when the server binds, registered before or after `listen()` ([ADR-00413](../adr/ADR-00413.md))<br>• `socket.setNoDelay`/`setKeepAlive` are real `setsockopt` calls — `setKeepAlive(enable, initialDelay)` honours the idle-time argument (`TCP_KEEPIDLE`, or `SIO_KEEPALIVE_VALS` on Windows) ([ADR-00760](../adr/ADR-00760.md))<br>• See [ADR-00358](../adr/ADR-00358.md)<br>• `isIP`/`isIPv4`/`isIPv6` match Node's strict parser, not the platform `inet_pton`: leading-zero v4 octets and >4-digit v6 groups rejected, `%zone` IDs accepted ([ADR-00457](../adr/ADR-00457.md)) |
| `dgram` | ✅ | • `udp4` only — no `udp6`<br>• No `'listening'`/`'error'` events, options object, or multicast<br>• Message listeners must be arrow/function-expression literals<br>• `socket.send(msg, port, host)` positional form only — no `(msg, offset, length, port, address, cb)` form; no `.setTTL()`/membership methods | • Surface: UDP sockets: `createSocket('udp4')`, `bind`, `address()`, `setBroadcast()`, `on('message')`, `send`, `close`<br>• Each socket's fd folds into the same `select()` event loop as `net`/`child_process` ([ADR-00327](../adr/ADR-00327.md))<br>• `.address()` reports the real bound `{ address, family, port }` via `getsockname` (the `bind(0)` ephemeral-port idiom); `.setBroadcast(flag)` is a real `setsockopt(SO_BROADCAST)` — required before sending to a broadcast address ([ADR-00581](../adr/ADR-00581.md))<br>• `'message'` fires with a Buffer and an rinfo `{ address, port }`; `send(msg, port, host)` resolves `host` (name or IP) via the `dns` helper<br>• `msg`/`send` payloads take a string/Buffer/ArrayBuffer/DataView |
| `tls` | ✅ | • **Blocking** TCP connect + TLS handshake on both sides (a slow peer stalls the loop), the same simplification `net.connect` makes<br>• OpenSSL-only (libssl) — a `-crypto=commoncrypto` build using `tls` is a clean compile error (Mac's CommonCrypto has no TLS API)<br>• Client options `{ rejectUnauthorized }` only — no client-cert / ALPN / `servername` override (SNI = the host)<br>• Server `{ cert, key }` are PEM **strings** only — one cert per server, no chain/passphrase, no `requestCert` | • Surface: TLS-wrapped sockets<br>• Options may be an object literal or a bound object value ([ADR-00413](../adr/ADR-00413.md))<br>• **Client** `tls.connect(port, host[, {rejectUnauthorized}][, onSecureConnect])` (cert verification + SNI on by default) and **server** `tls.createServer({ cert, key }, connectionListener)` (`.listen`/`.close`, per-connection `SSL_accept`) — both return **net-shaped** handles (an `SSL*` in the socket), so `.on('data')`/`.write()`/`.end()`/`.on('connection')` reuse the net machinery, routing through `SSL_read`/`SSL_write`. A handshake/verify failure throws a catchable `Error` ([TDD-00109](../tdd/TDD-00109.md)/[TDD-00110](../tdd/TDD-00110.md)/[ADR-00344](../adr/ADR-00344.md)/[ADR-00345](../adr/ADR-00345.md)) |
| `dns` | ✅ | • `dns.resolve4`/`resolve` use `getaddrinfo` (the OS resolver), not real DNS `A` queries — no `resolve6`/`resolveMx`/`resolveTxt`/`reverse`<br>• IPv4 (`AF_INET`) only; `family` is always 4<br>• The callback forms fire synchronously, not on a later event-loop tick<br>• Failure passes a generic `Error` (`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`), not a `code`-tagged Node error | • Surface: `dns.lookup`, `dns.resolve4`/`resolve`, `dns.promises.lookup`<br>• `getaddrinfo(3)`-backed ([ADR-00326](../adr/ADR-00326.md), [ADR-00329](../adr/ADR-00329.md)); `lookup` returns one dotted-quad, `resolve4` all A records as a `string[]`, `promises.lookup` a `Promise<{address, family}>`<br>• Verified on Mac (arm64) with the Darwin `struct addrinfo` `ai_addr`/`ai_next` offsets probed on the machine — the same layout the WebSocket-client resolver still gates out on Darwin |
| `zlib` | ✅ | • The callback form fires synchronously, not deferred to the next event-loop tick<br>• No Brotli (`brotliCompress*`) — it would pull in `-lbrotli`, a new system dependency this binding deliberately avoids<br>• No class/stream forms (`createGzip()`, `zlib.Gzip`, …) — the WHATWG `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream` cover the streaming case ([STREAMS.md](STREAMS.md))<br>• `{ level }` is the only supported option and must be a compile-time constant<br>• A decompressed result needs an explicit `: Buffer` annotation to call `.toString()` — the return type infers as a bare `Uint8Array`, so `zlib.gunzipSync(g).toString()` unannotated is a compile error | • Surface: `gzip`/`gunzip`, `deflate`/`inflate`, `deflateRaw`/`inflateRaw`, `unzip`, each `*Sync` + `(err, result)` callback<br>• One-shot calls over the same libz backend as `CompressionStream` ([ADR-00302](../adr/ADR-00302.md)), driven by a shared `@__kml_zlib_oneshot` helper ([ADR-00321](../adr/ADR-00321.md))<br>• Input may be a Buffer/TypedArray, ArrayBuffer, DataView, or string (UTF-8); output is always a Buffer |

| `http` client | ✅ | • `.abort()`/`.destroy()` cancel only a not-yet-fired request — an in-flight transfer isn't torn down<br>• `.on('error')` is accepted but never fired — transport failures throw instead<br>• `http.Agent`/`https.Agent` are inert — pool options are validated but configure nothing (one connection per request), `.destroy()` is a no-op, `.sockets`/`.requests` reject cleanly ([ADR-00432](../adr/ADR-00432.md))<br>• `headers` is literal-form-only; request-body chunks are strings only (`req.write()`/`req.end(body)`)<br>• `agent` is accepted and ignored — one connection per request (Node's `agent: false`), no pooling | • Surface: `http.get`/`http.request`<br>• Request bodies: `req.write(chunk)` stages a string chunk (appending across calls), `req.end([body])` appends a final chunk before firing, pairing with a `method: "POST"` option; response surface is `res.statusCode`/`res.on('data'/'end')`/`res.resume()`/`setEncoding`. Both calls return a ClientRequest handle (`request()` sends nothing until `.end()`). Options objects are literal or variable-bound, supporting `{ port, path, host/hostname, method, headers, agent }`. See [ADR-00575](../adr/ADR-00575.md), [ADR-00430](../adr/ADR-00430.md), [ADR-00429](../adr/ADR-00429.md), [ADR-00500](../adr/ADR-00500.md), [TDD-00138](../tdd/TDD-00138.md)<br>• libcurl-backed with async event-loop delivery, contextually-typed callbacks incl. `test` wrappers ([ADR-00404](../adr/ADR-00404.md)–[ADR-00406](../adr/ADR-00406.md), [ADR-00412](../adr/ADR-00412.md)) |
| `https` | ✅ | • `https.createServer` is HTTPS/1.1 only — an http/1.1-only ALPN forces even an h2-capable client to 1.1<br>• Inherits `http.createServer`'s V1 `res` subset and one-request-per-connection (`Connection: close`) posture<br>• Same V1 client surface and caveats as `http.get`/`request` ([TDD-00138](../tdd/TDD-00138.md)) | • Surface: `https.get`/`https.request` client + `https.createServer`<br>• `https.createServer({ cert, key }[, handler])` uses the same `(req, res)` core as `http.createServer`, with the connection fiber's socket I/O routed through per-fd `SSL_read`/`SSL_write` shims; streaming response bodies over TLS are supported. | `cluster` | ✅ | • Messages are strings; one listener per event; `'online'` fires from a queued microtask (the worker is exec'd by then), not a wire handshake<br>• No `cluster.on(...)` (cluster-level events), `cluster.workers` map, `cluster.disconnect()`, `setupPrimary()`(`setupMaster`)/`settings` ([TDD-00105](../tdd/TDD-00105.md)/[ADR-00331](../adr/ADR-00331.md))<br>• On Darwin, `SO_REUSEPORT` accept distribution is uneven (often one worker) — correctness holds, balancing differs from Linux's kernel load-balancing<br>• Can't be combined with Worker threads (same restriction as `http.listen({workers})`) | • Surface: `fork`, worker messaging, `isPrimary`/`isWorker`/`workerId`, `Worker.id`/`.process`<br>• Workers each bind the port via `SO_REUSEPORT`<br>• Unifies with `http.listen({ workers: N })`'s worker-id global — the primary stays in the event loop while workers live (their IPC handles), then blocks in `waitpid` as the backstop<br>• Workers carry the TDD-00141 fork IPC channel ([ADR-00427](../adr/ADR-00427.md)): `worker.send`/`.on('message'/'online'/'exit'/'close'/'error')`/`.disconnect()`/`.kill()`/`.destroy()`/`.process.pid`; in-worker `process.send`/`process.on('message')` |
| `http2` **module** | ✅ | • `http2.createServer`/`createSecureServer` `(req, res)` handlers don't receive the request body — `req.on('data')`/`req.stream()` isn't wired to the h2 body (the `klain:http` `http.listen` h2 path delivers it as one buffered `req.body` chunk; TDD-00218)<br>• `stream.close()`/`setEncoding`/`resume`/`pause` are accepted no-ops; responses are written when the handler returns (no mid-stream RST/flow control)<br>• Client `http2.connect` is h2c only — a TLS authority throws<br>• Client requests are body-less (END_STREAM at submit) — `req.write`/`end(body)` are clean rejections<br>• Client response `':status'` arrives as a *string* in the headers map (Node types it as a number); session/stream `'error'`/`'close'` listeners are accepted no-ops<br>• `getDefaultSettings`/`getPackedSettings`/`getUnpackedSettings`: the invalid-value `RangeError` taxonomy is not modeled<br>• `createSecureServer` h2 connections are served one-at-a-time (the TLS drive is blocking in the accept path)<br>• Server/client push streams are unsupported ([TDD-00139](../tdd/TDD-00139.md)) | • Surface: `http2.createServer`/`createSecureServer`/`connect`, `Http2Session`/`Http2Stream`<br>• Server-side Stages 1–2: `http2.createServer` on the http server handle serves **h2c** (also answers 1.1, a superset of Node); compat `.on('request', (req, res))` and the core streams API — `.on('stream', (stream, headers))` with pseudo-headers on the map, `stream.respond({ ':status', … })` incl. response headers, `.end`/`.write`. See [TDD-00139](../tdd/TDD-00139.md), [ADR-00414](../adr/ADR-00414.md), [ADR-00415](../adr/ADR-00415.md)<br>• Client (Stage 3): `http2.connect("http://…")` → session `.request({ ':path', ':method', headers… })` → stream `.on('response'\|'data'\|'end')`<br>• Stage 4: `http2.constants` compile-time namespace (header/method names, RFC 7540 error codes; unknown members reject cleanly); `getDefaultSettings`/`getPackedSettings`/`getUnpackedSettings` produce nghttp2 wire format<br>• `createSecureServer({ cert, key }[, handler])` serves **h2 over TLS**: each accepted fd is TLS-handshaken, ALPN selects `h2`, driving the same nghttp2 session as h2c over `SSL_read`/`SSL_write` shims; compat and `.on('stream')` APIs inherited unchanged. A client that doesn't negotiate `h2` is dropped after the handshake (Node's `allowHTTP1:false` default) unless `allowHTTP1: true` serves it over the HTTPS/1.1 fiber path. See [TDD-00111](../tdd/TDD-00111.md) Stage 3b, [ADR-00504](../adr/ADR-00504.md), [ADR-00505](../adr/ADR-00505.md)<br>• Transparent h2, no `http2` import needed: `fetch` negotiates h2 over TLS (ALPN); `http.listen` serves **h2c** (cleartext prior-knowledge) alongside 1.1, riding nghttp2 (`http2src/http2.c`, linked when `http.listen` is used), the h2 preface detected per-connection and dispatched through the shared 1.1 handler. h2-over-TLS is served explicitly via `http2.createSecureServer`; async handlers under h2 remain unsupported ([TDD-00111](../tdd/TDD-00111.md) Stage 3b, [ADR-00357](../adr/ADR-00357.md)) |
